rv.q: This is a fast, slick, spare production that rarely skimps on detail as it digs deep beneath the play's presentations of power, nationhood and, yes, pesky testosterone.
The result is a fine portrait of a flawed hero.
Henry seems a more dominant figure than ever.

This … is very much a Henry V for our times … It’s something of an antidote to the season’s prevailing bonhomie and tinsel, but this bold interpretation is well worth a visit from those interested in alternative histories and hidden motivations.

cn.t: Critics praise Law's complex, mature portrayal and Roughan's bold, stripped-down production that reframes the play as a chilling study of power's corrupting influence rather than heroic jingoism, though some find it slow to expose emotional consequences.
